install.title: Pick a client. Start your task.
install.description: Native clients for local development, or a browser workspace without installation. Bring your own model API.
install.web.title: No download. Just open it.
install.web.detail: Works in desktop and mobile browsers. Files and conversation history are saved on your device; content needed for model requests is sent to your chosen API.
install.web.limits: No local shell in the browser. Your API must support CORS, or use your own relay.
install.web.step1.detail: Enter an API URL, model, and API key. Optionally remember the configuration in this browser.
install.web.step2.detail: Upload files or describe a task. Preview HTML, edit files, and export ZIPs.
install.web.step3.detail: Choose “Install app” in a supported desktop browser. On iPhone Safari: Share → Add to Home Screen. Installation does not bypass CORS.
install.native.detail: No development environment needed. Extract and run; installation is optional.
install.native.step1.detail: Verify and extract, then run in a terminal in the extracted folder. The workspace defaults to the current directory.
install.native.step2: First launch guides you through setup
install.native.step2.detail: First launch offers optional user installation and PATH setup. Then configure the API URL, model and key to enter the session. Existing configuration is preserved; no separate setup/start commands. Key input is hidden.
install.native.step3: Optional: install to run i in any project
install.native.step3.detail: Skip this if you accepted installation on first launch. Otherwise use the command below to install and update your user PATH. Open a new terminal, enter your project and type i. No silent installation or configuration replacement.
install.macos.note: Apple Silicon only, not universal. Not signed or notarized; verify the source. Build from source on Intel Macs.
install.linux.note: For Linux x86_64. Requires system TLS / OpenSSL libraries. Build from source for other architectures.
install.windows.note: For Windows x86_64. Extract the ZIP and run in PowerShell. This is not a graphical installer.

boundary.title: Your connections. Clear boundaries.
security.summary: Local workspace. Your model API. No API key storage on our servers.
security.link: See the data flow and security boundaries →
security.intro: Local storage is not local inference. Know what stays on your device and what is sent out.
boundary.data.detail: In direct mode, keys and model requests go to your chosen API, not our backend. Your own Relay routes them through your server. Task messages, selected file content, and images are sent to that model service.
boundary.credentials.detail: Optionally save keys in this browser’s localStorage, or keep them in memory only. This is not an encrypted vault: same-origin scripts or privileged browser extensions may read saved keys. Do not remember keys on shared devices.
boundary.plugins.detail: WASM plugins have no direct interface to the DOM, localStorage, or connection settings. The host grants file access and private storage by permission; plugins can see the input you give them. Native workers are trusted processes, not sandboxed.
boundary.preview.detail: HTML previews use an isolated iframe without host same-origin access. Enable JavaScript only for trusted content; scripts can read files in the preview snapshot. The browser disables local shell, but generated content is not automatically safe.
security.extension: Install only trusted browser extensions. Preflight repair uses the privileged debugger and may receive authentication metadata for matching requests. It is not the isolated WASM plugin system.
boundary.keys.detail: Direct requests go to your chosen API; your own Relay passes them through your server. Optionally remember keys in this browser.
boundary.files.detail: Persistent workspaces use local OPFS, separate from temporary /tmp. Clearing site data deletes workspaces. Export ZIP backups.
boundary.cors.detail: Direct mode needs API CORS support, your own relay, or a desktop extension. PWA does not bypass CORS. Extensions do not fix authentication or TLS.
